filename: Efficient first-order algorithms for large-scale, non-smooth maximum entropy models with application to wildfire science.pdf
title: Efficient first-order algorithms for large-scale, non-smooth maximum entropy models with application to wildfire science
code_availability: Not explicitly stated for the proposed MATLAB NPDHG implementation; WUMI dataset and SMLFire1.0 package available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7277980
testbed_rationale: The study focuses on optimization methods for statistical Maximum Entropy density estimation of regional wildfire occurrences, not Earth system model parameterization or physical process emulation.
pain_points: Computational scaling bottlenecks: estimating optimal stepsizes for classical first-order optimization requires O(min(m^2 n, mn^2)) operations, which is prohibitive for large feature/sample matrices
Coordinate descent solvers like GLMNET rely on logistic regression approximations (IWLR) that can fail to converge or give unreliable numerical solutions on dense ecological data
Lack of parallelism in state-of-the-art coordinate descent algorithms
Non-smooth regularizations (elastic net, group lasso, l-infinity) lack smoothness required for standard quasi-Newton or second-order methods
extraction_notes: Author Jérôme Darbon was spelled with accents in the original paper. The paper applies machine learning (Maxent density estimation and Random Forests for prior construction) to ecological and wildfire data in the western US. Support is acknowledged from NSF LEAP STC Award #2019625 for co-author Jatan Buch.
